newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenyan tea output still rising in first 7 months.
newsitem.headline: Kenyan tea output still rising in first 7 months.

text.p: Kenyan tea production rose 6.44 percent in the first seven months of this year over the same period in 1995, a leading brokerage said on Tuesday.
In a report, Africa Tea Brokers (ATB) put production in the month of July at 17,344,865 kg, an increase of 1,114,518 kg or 6.8 percent over the same month in 1995.
"The cumulative figure (January-July) now stands at 151.68 million kg, an increase of 9.18 million kg or 6.44 percent over the same period in the previous year," Africa Tea Brokers said.

"The weather in most tea growing areas has been dry with only intermittent rainfall which increased towards the end of the month (July). With warmer temperatures, the crop has shown progressive improvement," the brokers added.

Four sales were held in July when a total of 214,478 packages were sold at an average price of $1.41 per kg. Comparative figures for the same month last year were 248,783 packages sold at an average price of $1.25.

"With often improved quality, brighter teas of all descriptions were generally fully firm to dearer," the brokers said. "On balance, most teas gained 2-4 U.S. cents." --Nairobi Newsroom ++254-2 330-261
